bullets.title: BOJ raises rates to 31-year high; yen weakens despite hike
bullets.body: Bank of Japan raised its overnight call rate 25bp to 1.25%, the highest level since 1995. Despite the hike, the yen weakened as forward guidance disappointed markets; BOJ Governor Ueda declined to rule out any policy options but warned large/repeated hikes risk overshooting. BOJ is monitoring Middle East developments, AI demand, and FX volatility as inflation risks.

bullets.title: US 10-year yield at 5%; 2-year surges to 4.74%; forward 2s top 5%
bullets.body: US 10-year Treasury yield hit 5% with 30-year above 5.30%, while the 2-year surged to 4.74% — its highest since July 2024. One-year forward 2s are topping 5%, and market is pricing an 84% probability of a 2026 Fed rate hike with Goldman Sachs now expecting an October hike one week before the midterms.

bullets.title: Fed's Schmid: Economy strong; supports hike as inflation trends above 3%
bullets.body: Fed's Schmid backed the recent rate hike and said inflation data suggests a trend above 3%. He agrees with Warsh that AI investment is driving capital demand and geopolitical challenges are lifting bond yields. He characterizes the labor market as in balance.

bullets.title: Goldman: Hyperscaler gross debt issuance to surge to $420B in 2027
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs forecasts $420B in global investment-grade debt issuance directly from hyperscalers in 2027 — up 60%+ from ~$250B in 2026 — driven by higher CapEx revisions. Hyperscaler debt will equal roughly half of all new Treasury long-duration borrowing in 2027.

bullets.title: NVDA CEO expects to double chip sales YoY; DLSS 5 momentum
bullets.body: Jensen Huang stated he expects NVIDIA to sell twice as many chips next year versus the current year. Separately, DLSS 5 and path tracing integration in Dark Souls 3 showcases next-gen visual capability. Tech calls seen as cheap with low IV ranks (≤7) at 90th-percentile skew, making NVDA a highlighted upside play.

bullets.title: META's Muse AI hits #1 on Apple App Store globally, surpassing ChatGPT
bullets.body: META's new AI agent Muse reached #1 on the US Apple App Store free apps ranking, ahead of ChatGPT. Multiple fintwit accounts flagged this as evidence of strong consumer traction and argued that if META dominates the personal AI agent market it becomes the ultimate gatekeeper for top-of-funnel discovery and high-intent commerce.

bullets.title: Memory prices surged 5-7x; shortage expected to worsen through 2027
bullets.body: Intel's CEO warned at the AI Infra Summit that memory prices have jumped 5-7x, now comprising ~75% of costs for lower-end phones and laptops. SK Hynix flagged 2027 as potentially the worst supply year; MU reportedly holds $100B in take-or-pay contracts. RBC channel checks project 80-100% HBM ASP hikes for 2027.

bullets.title: INTC +9.8%, MRVL +5.4% as Treasury yields ease post-Fed hike
bullets.body: Following the Fed's 25bp hike, Treasury yields fell to 4.949%, lifting semiconductor stocks. INTC surged 9.8% on a report of a potential US memory chip manufacturing deal with SK Hynix; MRVL gained 5.4%. Barclays also initiated TSEM with a 41% upside target, citing its well-placed silicon photonics position.

bullets.title: AMD: QA gap vs. CUDA flagged; chip price hike ~10% in Q4 on TSMC costs
bullets.body: vLLM's Kevin Lu blog highlighted AMD's lack of stable QA clusters creates 'order-of-magnitude worse' software quality vs. CUDA — a structural software reliability concern. Separately, ChannelGate reports AMD will raise chip prices ~10% in Q4 due to TSMC cost increases.

bullets.title: TSMC: Sub-1.4nm fab approval; plans three Longtan fabs by 2030 for >$31B
bullets.body: TSMC secured regulatory approval for sub-1.4nm manufacturing plants and plans to build three new fabs in Longtan, north Taiwan, with the first targeted for mass production by 2030 at a cost exceeding NT$1 trillion (~$31.4B). TSMC is also delaying high-NA EUV adoption to 2030 pending 12-inch mask supply chain maturity at ~80% readiness.

bullets.title: Apple iPhone 18 Pro officially released; Apple suing OpenAI; US-China summit angle
bullets.body: Apple's iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max launched officially. Tim Cook is attending the Trump-Xi state dinner alongside Jensen Huang and Sam Altman. Separately, Apple is reportedly suing OpenAI and competing with Google to own the personal assistant market. A US-China summit Sept 24 is expected to yield AI/semiconductor deals; Apple is reportedly testing CXMT products.

bullets.title: Intel 14A process under evaluation by Amazon, Apple, AMD, Google, Tesla, Microsoft, NVIDIA, Qualcomm
bullets.body: Intel's 14A process node is reportedly being evaluated by most major hyperscalers and chipmakers. No adoption decision yet, but the breadth of evaluators signals strategic interest in foundry diversification.

bullets.title: CXMT enters NAND flash; competitive threat to SNDK flagged
bullets.body: Chinese DRAM giant CXMT plans to build a 3D NAND R&D production line at its second Beijing fab (2-3 years out). SNDK saw a significant AM selloff on the news, with one trader noting a large sell order expected in tonight's SMH rebalance. SK Hynix's Solidigm is also reportedly planning a US NAND fab.

bullets.title: Aramco suspends European crude allocations; Red Sea traffic down 67% from 2024 avg
bullets.body: Saudi Aramco told at least two European refiners they will receive no crude next month due to attacks on the Red Sea pipeline. Weekly traffic through Bab El-Mandeb since early August is running below one-third of the 2024 seven-day average. Strait of Hormuz commodity vessel traffic fell to just 4 on Thursday vs. a 10-day average of 16.

bullets.title: Semis testing 50-DMA for 3rd time; Goldman warns CTAs are sellers in all scenarios next week
bullets.body: The semiconductor sector is testing its 50-day moving average resistance for the third time with unclear breakout odds. Goldman's flow desk warns CTAs are positioned as sellers in all scenarios next week amid a rising Panic Index and slumping sentiment.

bullets.title: $7T quad-witching (2nd largest ever) hits amid SPY near $3.7B put wall at 760
bullets.body: Today's quad-witching event involves $7 trillion in notional value, the 2nd largest on record. SPY has returned to a $3.7B put wall at the 760 strike just ahead of the expiry, creating a technically sensitive setup.

bullets.title: AI pause calls triggered hardware selloff, but no actual lab slowdown confirmed
bullets.body: After Dario Amodei called for slowing frontier AI development (backed by Altman and Musk), AI hardware stocks sold off. However, interviews with frontier lab representatives suggest no actual development pause is occurring. Only 3% of US consumers currently pay for AI, highlighting the monetization runway ahead.

bullets.title: Warren Buffett steps down as Berkshire chairman; Howard Buffett takes over
bullets.body: Warren Buffett stepped down as Berkshire Hathaway chairman effective immediately, moving to chairman emeritus. Son Howard G. Buffett takes over the chair role. Greg Abel's succession as CEO is reaffirmed.

bullets.title: MRVL expands GlobalFoundries deal for AI optical networking; VIAV flagged as CPO testing bottleneck play
bullets.body: Marvell and GlobalFoundries expanded their multi-year chip-capacity agreement for U.S. AI data-center optical networking. Silicon photonics CPO testing remains a bottleneck 6 months on, with VIAV and LITE cited as optical test equipment beneficiaries. Tower Semiconductor began high-volume shipments of 800G/1.6T optical engines with NewPhotonics.

bullets.title: Waymo (GOOGL) announces Singapore robotaxi launch for 2028; PLTR building Chipotle food safety platform
bullets.body: Waymo plans to begin commercial robotaxi operations in Singapore by 2028 with mapping starting in early 2027. Palantir is building a Foundry-hosted food safety risk platform for Chipotle, aggregating health inspection, pest, and illness data to flag restaurant-level risk.
